summary: Cohort epoch synchronization failure creating intermittent split-variant routing during staged rollout
description:
Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout that should have preserved model-version pinning for a subset of NorthBridge Media tenants, a synchronization mismatch between the rollout epoch recorded by the control-plane orchestrator and the edge-proxy cohort table led to intermittent traffic being split across two model variants. Impact: ~3-5% of the customer's requests received responses from an unintended variant, producing observable quality regressions in the customer's production evaluation set and a small number of API signature mismatches for structured outputs. This occurred during a low-traffic window but affected production user-facing inference for a small cohort.

Observed behavior: Some sessions that were expected to remain pinned to the older model variant were routed to the new canary variant for several minutes before failing back. The routing decision logs show inconsistent epoch IDs between the orchestrator snapshot and the edge in-memory cohort map. No GPU exhaustion or autoscaler events were observed.

Expected behavior: Cohort epoch values should be atomically advanced across the control plane and all edge instances so that pinned sessions retain affinity unless an intentional reassign/eviction occurs.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Initiate a staged canary rollout with cohort weighting (10% canary) and model version pinning enabled for tenant namespace NB-*/priority routes.
2) Allow the orchestrator to publish epoch=E+1 snapshot and confirm push succeeded to config service.
3) Trigger a controlled connection shuffle at the edge by restarting a subset of edge-proxies in us-east for routine maintenance.
4) Observe session routing for pinned tenants during the 2-10 minute window after edge restart; compare orchestrator epoch vs edge cohort epoch and inspect model variant assignments.
5) Reproduce by toggling the deploy with a small canary weight and repeating edge restart to surface the mismatch consistently.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: edge local cache TTL allowed a stale epoch to persist across an edge restart, causing temporary divergence in routing decisions.
Found that config push to CDN cache layer recorded success but edge instances pulling from CDN occasionally returned 304 with stale cache due to GC race in the CDN edge cache layer (region us-east).

Edge restart timing with in-flight session handoffs exposed a race between session-store lease renewal and cohort epoch reconcile path, allowing a short window where session affinity rules were evaluated against outdated epoch metadata.
No evidence of autoscaler or GPU preemption; serving-runtime metrics normal. Tokenization and output parsing errors correlate with model mismatch rather than model corruption.
Reproduced locally by simulating delayed snapshot propagation (delay ~6s) plus immediate edge restart; variant-splitting reproduced deterministically under those timings.
comments: Ava Martinez (support): Customer reported inconsistent outputs from their pinned sessions around 02:15 UTC. Customer provided sample request IDs and an eval set showing degraded ROUGE for 4% of requests.
Ravi Patel (oncall eng): Confirmed epoch mismatch in routing logs for edge-proxy-7b4a. Rolled an emergency config push to force cohort refresh on all us-east edges at 02:18 UTC.
NorthBridge SRE (customer): Noted they saw oddness correlated with our maintenance restart window. Thank you for quick action, please advise on root cause and mitigation plan.

Ravi Patel (oncall eng): Temporary mitigation applied: manual cohort resync and a small increase to edge cache TTL safety window to avoid immediate stale reads during orchestrator publishes. Scheduling a patch to the route-coordinator to enforce single-phase commit across snapshot publish and edge acknowledging path.
CS Manager (Jordan Li): Customer-facing note prepared; CS team to follow up with NorthBridge with timeline for permanent fix and offer a credit for affected window.
resolution_notes: Workaround: manual cohort resync executed 2026-02-18T02:18 UTC which restored epoch coherence across edge fleet; temporary guardrail added to prevent edge restarts within 30s of snapshot publish. Root cause: race between CDN-backed config propagation and edge restart causing stale epoch reads. Remediation: patch to route-coordinator that implements an atomic publish-ack protocol and stronger edge-side TTL validation scheduled and PR opened (see related_github_prs). Post-incident follow-up: runbook update, monitoring alert added for epoch divergence. Customer notified and offered usage credit.
next_steps: Complete PR for atomic publish-ack protocol and land in canary cluster (owner: Ravi Patel, ETA: 2026-02-24)
Add a synthetic monitor that asserts epoch parity between orchestrator and a sample of edges every minute (owner: Observability team, ETA: 2026-02-21)
Update rollout runbook to include 'no edge restarts within snapshot window' recommendation and automated enforcement option (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-02-22)
